## Parameter Sensitivity Analysis

<!-- Auto-generated by src/powergrid_benchmark/mintou_planning_sensitivity.py (status: public_simbench_planning_sensitivity_v1). Numbers match evidence/tables/real_sensitivity_sweep.csv. -->

To verify that the comparison on the base proxy configuration does not hinge on a fortunate parameter choice, we performed a one-at-a-time parameter sweep around the default optimizer settings. CARS-MODE exposes two influential parameters: the population size $N_p$ (shared by all population-based competitors) and the jDE resampling probability $\tau$, i.e., the per-individual probability of redrawing the self-adaptive scale factor $F$ and crossover rate $CR$ in each generation. The remaining mechanisms (two-strategy pool, budget repair, crowding diversity) are binary switches already covered by the ablation study. Since the original implementation hardcoded $\tau=0.1$, we exposed it as a configuration parameter whose default reproduces the archived behaviour exactly, and swept it over $\{0.05, 0.1, 0.2\}$; $N_p$ was swept over $\{20, 40, 60\}$ (default 40).

Each parameter point was re-run with 10 independent seeds under the protocol of the main experiments: identical SimBench-derived problem instance, identical search/evaluation scenario seeds, and the hypervolume of the feasible non-dominated front computed under the same fixed, method-independent normalization bounds, so hypervolumes are directly comparable across parameter points. On the population-size axis the strongest baseline (NSGA-II) was re-run at each matched population size; for the method-specific parameters, which do not affect the baselines, the NSGA-II reference at the default $N_p=40$ is shown. Two-sided Mann-Whitney U tests compare the proposed method against the corresponding NSGA-II reference at every point.

Figure \ref{fig:sensitivity} (panels (a) and (b)) and Table \ref{tab:sensitivity} summarize the sweep.

| Parameter | Value | CARS-MODE HV (mean $\pm$ std) | NSGA-II reference HV | $p$ (MWU) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| population size $N_p$ | 20 | 0.0382 $\pm$ 0.0018 | 0.0329 | 0.00100798 |
| population size $N_p$ | 40 (default) | 0.0409 $\pm$ 0.0016 | 0.0385 | 0.00579536 |
| population size $N_p$ | 60 | 0.0425 $\pm$ 0.0007 | 0.0399 | 0.000182672 |
| jDE resampling probability $\tau$ | 0.05 | 0.0407 $\pm$ 0.0008 | 0.0385 | 0.00058284 |
| jDE resampling probability $\tau$ | 0.1 (default) | 0.0410 $\pm$ 0.0016 | 0.0385 | 0.00361051 |
| jDE resampling probability $\tau$ | 0.2 | 0.0416 $\pm$ 0.0011 | 0.0385 | 0.000182672 |

Across the population size $N_p$ axis, the mean hypervolume of CARS-MODE varies between 0.0382 and 0.0425 (a spread of 10.5% of the default-configuration value), with the best mean at population size = 60.

Across the jDE resampling probability $\tau$ axis, the mean hypervolume of CARS-MODE varies between 0.0407 and 0.0416 (a spread of 2.3% of the default-configuration value), with the best mean at jDE resampling probability = 0.2.

At every parameter point the mean sampled-bound/clipped hypervolume of CARS-MODE remains above the corresponding NSGA-II reference (smallest margin 0.0022 in absolute hypervolume), i.e., no rank reversal occurs within this exploratory sweep and metric. The nominal advantage has two-sided Mann--Whitney $p < 0.05$ at every point, without multiplicity correction across the sweep. The total spread of CARS-MODE's mean hypervolume across all six parameter points is 10.5% of the default-configuration value. This supports local parameter robustness for the archived metric only; it is not a normalization-robustness result, because the analytic-bound and common-reference diagnostics reported in Section 6.7 change the broader method ordering. The defaults ($N_p = 40$, $\tau = 0.1$) are not the best observed points in the tested grid.
